cases.sentence: Лицо ее блестело ___; но блеск этот был не веселый – он напоминал страшный блеск пожара среди темной ночи.
cases.explain: «ярким блеском» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Anna came in with hanging head, playing with the tassels of her hood. Her face was brilliant and glowing; but this glow was not one of brightness; it suggested the fearful glow of a conflagration in the midst of a dark night. On seeing her husband, Anna raised her head and smiled, as though she had just waked up.

cases.sentence: Она чувствовала, что какая-то ___ помогала ей и поддерживала ее.
cases.explain: «невидимая сила» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Anna said what came to her lips, and marveled, hearing herself, at her own capacity for lying. How simple and natural were her words, and how likely that she was simply sleepy! She felt herself clad in an impenetrable armor of falsehood. She felt that some unseen force had come to her aid and was supporting her.

cases.sentence: – Я хочу предостеречь тебя в том, – сказал он ___, – что по неосмотрительности и легкомыслию ты можешь подать в свете повод говорить о тебе.
cases.explain: «тихим голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I want to warn you,” he said in a low voice, “that through thoughtlessness and lack of caution you may cause yourself to be talked about in society. Your too animated conversation this evening with Count Vronsky” (he enunciated the name firmly and with deliberate emphasis) “attracted attention.”

cases.sentence: Я признаю, как ты знаешь, ревность чувством оскорбительным и унизительным и никогда не позволю себе руководиться этим чувством; но есть ___ приличия, которые нельзя преступать безнаказанно.
cases.explain: «известные законы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “This is what I meant to say to you,” he went on coldly and composedly, “and I beg you to listen to it. I consider jealousy, as you know, a humiliating and degrading feeling, and I shall never allow myself to be influenced by it; but there are certain rules of decorum which cannot be disregarded with impunity. This evening it was not I observed it, but judging by the impression made on the company, everyone observed that your conduct and deportment were not altogether what could be desired.”

cases.sentence: Она говорила и удивлялась тому натурально-спокойному, ___, которым она говорила, и выбору слов, которые она употребляла.
cases.explain: «верному тону» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: She spoke, and marveled at the confident, calm, and natural tone in which she was speaking, and the choice of the words she used.

cases.sentence: На мгновение лицо ее опустилось, и потухла ___ во взгляде; но слово «люблю» опять возмутило ее.
cases.explain: «насмешливая искра» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: For an instant her face fell, and the mocking gleam in her eyes died away; but the word love threw her into revolt again. She thought: “Love? Can he love? If he hadn’t heard there was such a thing as love, he would never have used the word. He doesn’t even know what love is.”

cases.sentence: Но я говорю не о себе; ___ тут – наш сын и ты сама.
cases.explain: «главные лица» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Pardon, let me say all I have to say. I love you. But I am not speaking of myself; the most important persons in this matter are our son and yourself. It may very well be, I repeat, that my words seem to you utterly unnecessary and out of place; it may be that they are called forth by my mistaken impression. In that case, I beg you to forgive me. But if you are conscious yourself of even the smallest foundation for them, then I beg you to think a little, and if your heart prompts you, to speak out to me. …”

cases.sentence: Она долго лежала неподвижно с ___, блеск которых, ей казалось, она сама в темноте видела.
cases.explain: «открытыми глазами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “It’s late, it’s late,” she whispered with a smile. A long while she lay, not moving, with open eyes, whose brilliance she almost fancied she could herself see in the darkness.
